Slide.Title: name (noun)
Slide.SlideText: name (noun) Definition: Definition: a word by which a person, animal, or thing is known or called Synonyms: Synonyms: alias, handle (informal), heading, title Examples: Examples: What is Mr. Johnson’s first name? Their family name is written on their mailbox. You can put your name on a nametag. You can put your name on a nametag.

Slide.Title: name (verb)
Slide.SlideText: name (verb) Definition: Definition: to appoint; to nominate; to give a name to Synonyms: Synonyms: call, designate Examples: Examples: She named the baby after her grandmother. He named his dog Rex. He was named the head of the organization after the director retired. He was named the head of the organization after the director retired.

Slide.Title: nation (noun)
Slide.SlideText: nation (noun) Definition: Definition: a country, together with its social and political systems Synonyms: Synonyms: country, people, society Examples: Examples: The nation recently declared its independence. Our nation is very fond of baseball. Mexico is a nation that borders the United States. Mexico is a nation that borders the United States.

Slide.Title: nature (noun)
Slide.SlideText: nature (noun) Definition: Definition: the physical world, including all natural processes and living things Synonyms: Synonyms: outdoors Examples: Examples: In many places, nature is threatened by human activity. Ancient people lived close to nature. In these mountains, nature is at its best. In these mountains, nature is at its best.

Slide.Title: navy (noun)
Slide.SlideText: navy (noun) Definition: Definition: the part of a country’s military force trained to fight at sea Synonyms: Synonyms: fleet, armada, flotilla, military Examples: Examples: The navy defends our seacoast. She joined the navy after finishing college. Officers of the navy wear white uniforms. Officers of the navy wear white uniforms.

Slide.Title: neighbor (noun)
Slide.SlideText: neighbor (noun) Definition: Definition: a person or country that is next to or near another Synonyms: Synonyms: friend, associate Examples: Examples: Mexico is a neighbor of the United States. Our neighbors often play loud music at night. Some neighbors are very noisy. Some neighbors are very noisy.

Slide.Title: nerve (noun)
Slide.SlideText: nerve (noun) Definition: Definition: a thin piece of tissue that sends information through the body to and from the brain; 2) presumption Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) sensory apparatus; 2) audacity, insolence Examples: Examples: He had the nerve to yell at the judge. (audacity) These bundles of nerves convey messages from the brain to the rest of the body. (sensory apparatus) These bundles of nerve fibers convey impulses from the brain to the rest of the body.

Slide.Title: new (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: new (adjective) Definition: Definition: not existing before; recently made; different Synonyms: Synonyms: fresh, modern Examples: Examples: This idea is totally new to me. The colleagues find the new technology hard to master. The teenager is showing off his new car. The teenager is showing off his new car.

Slide.Title: news (noun)
Slide.SlideText: news (noun) Definition: Definition: information about recent events, especially as reported by the media Synonyms: Synonyms: announcement, broadcast, information, message, report Examples: Examples: It’s time for the news on Channel 79. News of the recent blast is all over the radio. News can be accessed on your computer. News can be accessed on your computer.

Slide.Title: night (noun)
Slide.SlideText: night (noun) Definition: Definition: the time between the setting and rising of the sun when there is little or no light Synonyms: Synonyms: evening, dark Examples: Examples: It is expected to rain all night tonight. Are they arriving at ten o’clock in the morning or at night? Most people enjoy starry, peaceful nights. Most people enjoy starry, peaceful nights.

Slide.Title: noise (noun)
Slide.SlideText: noise (noun) Definition: Definition: sound, especially when loud Synonyms: Synonyms: bang, blast, sound, uproar Examples: Examples: There’s a lot of noise in a typical city. The children will wake up if you make noise. Oh, please, stop that noise! Oh, please, stop that noise!

Slide.Title: noon (noun)
Slide.SlideText: noon (noun) Definition: Definition: the middle of the day; twelve o’clock in the daytime Synonyms: Synonyms: midday Examples: Examples: Will it start snowing at noon or later? The flight is expected to arrive at noon. It’s almost noon; let’s go to lunch. It’s almost noon; let’s go to lunch.

Slide.Title: north (noun)
Slide.SlideText: north (noun) Definition: Definition: the direction to the left of a person facing the rising sun; opposite of “south” Synonyms: Synonyms: arctic, polar, upward Examples: Examples: I was born in the north, but now I live in Florida. There’s a cold wind from the north. The compass points to the north. The compass points to the north.

Slide.Title: not (adverb)
Slide.SlideText: not (adverb) Definition: Definition: a word conveying the general meaning of “no,” often used to express refusal or negation Synonyms: Synonyms: no, negative, never Examples: Examples: She is not fond of pets. You are not allowed to turn left on this street. This is the wrong way; do not enter here. This is the wrong way; do not enter here.

Slide.Title: note (noun)
Slide.SlideText: note (noun) Definition: Definition: a word or words written to help a person remember; a short letter Synonyms: Synonyms: letter, memo, message Examples: Examples: “I will send your teacher a note to excuse your absence,” said the mother. The mailman left a note on our door. Send them a thank-you note for their hospitality. Send them a thank-you note for their hospitality.

Slide.Title: note (verb)
Slide.SlideText: note (verb) Definition: Definition: to talk about something already known Synonyms: Synonyms: attend to, observe, mention Examples: Examples: He noted in his report that the stock market was a factor in the company’s failure. The audience members noted that the speaker looked tired. The audience members noted that the speaker looked tired.

Slide.Title: now (adverb)
Slide.SlideText: now (adverb) Definition: Definition: at this time, immediately Synonyms: Synonyms: currently, presently Examples: Examples: They are expected any minute now. The book is now ready for publication. If not now, when do you plan to start the project? If not now, when do you plan to start the project?

Slide.Title: nuclear (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: nuclear (adjective) Definition: Definition: about the energy produced or about weapons that explode by using energy from atoms. Synonyms: Synonyms: atomic Examples: Examples: The world is worried about the nuclear capabilities of Iran and North Korea. Nuclear energy is produced by splitting atoms or by bringing them together. Nuclear energy is produced by splitting atoms or by bringing them together.

Slide.Title: nutrition (noun)
Slide.SlideText: nutrition (noun) Definition: Definition: any food or substance that makes plants, humans, or animals grow Synonyms: Synonyms: nourishment Examples: Examples: Nutrition is inadequate in some poor areas. There isn’t much nutrition in potato chips. Information about nutrition is available on most packaged foods. Information about nutrition is available on most packaged foods.

Slide.Title: number (noun)
Slide.SlideText: number (noun) Definition: Definition: a word or sign used to show the order or amount of things Synonyms: Synonyms: numeral Examples: Examples: I don’t know her telephone number. The number of stars in the sky is infinite. Can you add these numbers? Can you add these numbers?
